**Memory Complexity:** $O(W \times H \times D)$ bits, packed into $O(W \times H)$ texels [S2, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the core data structure is a 'slicemap', which is a 2D texture (O(W x H) texels). It further explains that the k-th bit of the RGBA representation of a pixel encodes the voxel value at grid coordinates (i, j, k). Since RGBA has 4 channels and typically 8 bits per channel, this allows packing 32 bits (voxels) per texel. Therefore, a 3D volume of size W x H x D requires O(W x H) texels to store, with the memory complexity proportional to the number of bits packed, which corresponds to the volume size O(W x H x D) bits.
